# AutoFirma

`app-crypt/autofirma` builds the desktop client and configurator from the
upstream `v1.9.2` tag, with the two upstream fixes also used by AUR:

- `05d433f6d5439263c5cf58bbd1391e06d5fc6bea`: Firefox profile locations.
- `cb08ba7960dab42d0965cfce8c763fe354232f14`: exclude symmetric NSS keys from
  the signing certificate selection.

As checked on 9 November 2026, `v1.9.2` is the latest upstream tag. The
repository does not publish GitHub Releases. Its `master` POM still declares
1.9.1 despite containing later changes, so the package uses the fixed tag.

## Build

Java-WebSocket is compiled from commit
`8c5766a293c2dd3e0d035c0e0d70f88f57235fa8`. AutoFirma is then built with both
`env-dev` and `env-install` profiles, selecting the desktop/configurator
reactor and setting `clienteafirma.version=1.9.2`. This builds all required
AutoFirma modules together instead of consuming the older internal 1.9 JARs
selected by upstream's default install profile.

The build uses JDK 17 and `dev-java/maven-bin:3.9`. The offline dependency
archive contains 683 original third-party JAR and POM files from Maven Central.
These are precompiled library/build-tool dependencies. No compiled AutoFirma
modules or Java-WebSocket artifacts are included in the dependency archive.

Every external artifact is pinned by SHA-256 in
[the Maven inventory](../maven-bundles/autofirma-1.9.2.json). Fixed local metadata
is generated from those reviewed versions to resolve Maven version ranges
offline. Mutable remote version metadata and personal Maven settings are not
used. Both Java-WebSocket and AutoFirma are compiled with Maven's `--offline`.

The [dependency Release](https://github.com/Isaac-Martinez-Forte/esparto-overlay/releases/tag/sources-autofirma-1.9.2)
is regenerated by GitHub Actions and checked against the reviewed archive hash.
The ebuild fetches five files in total: two source archives, two patches and
one offline Maven repository.

## Install

If migrating from `autofirma-bin`, first remove its explicit world entry:

```sh
sudo emerge --deselect app-crypt/autofirma-bin
```

This changes the selected package list and leaves the installed binary in
place while the source package builds. It avoids a conflict when Portage
tries to keep an explicitly selected binary package installed.

For an existing Esparto checkout, accept the experimental version and install:

```sh
printf '%s\n' 'app-crypt/autofirma::esparto ~amd64' |
  sudo tee -a /etc/portage/package.accept_keywords/autofirma
sudo emerge --ask --verbose '=app-crypt/autofirma-1.9.2-r1::esparto'
```

This assumes `package.accept_keywords` is a directory. If it is a file, add
the same keyword entry there. The package blocks `app-crypt/autofirma-bin`
because both install the same application launcher and desktop entry;
After deselecting the binary package, Portage can remove it as part of the
replacement.

The installed commands are `autofirma` and `autofirma-configurator`.
The desktop entry handles `afirma://` links.

## Browser setup

Revision `1.9.2-r1` prepares browser communication automatically whenever
`autofirma` is launched, including launches through an `afirma://` link.
Run it as your normal desktop user.

The launcher invokes `autofirma-browser-setup` before the Gentoo Java launcher.
It creates a private TLS identity under `~/.afirma/Autofirma` if none exists,
using AutoFirma's expected PKCS#12 alias and password. Existing PKCS#12 files
are reused; their CA is recovered from the chain when needed. Private keys
are readable only by the user. Temporary CA signing keys are removed after
generation.

The CA is imported into existing Firefox profiles found in both legacy and
XDG configuration directories, the Snap Firefox location, and the user's
shared NSS databases used by Chromium-family browsers. Both relative and
absolute Firefox profile paths are supported. The helper uses a fingerprinted
nickname and does not delete other certificates. It does not recreate an
existing TLS identity or re-import an already present CA on every launch.
New browser profiles are picked up on subsequent launches.

If a running browser prevents a trust update, the launcher reports the error;
close the browser and launch AutoFirma again. Local document signing remains
available if browser initialization fails. An invalid existing PKCS#12 file
is reported instead of being silently replaced.

Certificate stores are configured per user at application startup, not during
the root package installation. There is no system-wide trust installation.
The optional upstream `autofirma-configurator` command and **Tools → Restore
installation** remain available for explicit repairs.

The desktop handler was checked with `xdg-mime query default
x-scheme-handler/afirma`, which returned `autofirma.desktop` on the test system.
An actual signing transaction on an electronic administration website has not
been tested by the packaging checks.

## Validation

A clean Portage build completed offline using the final dependency archive,
including Java-WebSocket, all 33 AutoFirma reactor projects, the smoke test and
installation into a staging directory. Portage also fetched the public Release
archive into a fresh directory and verified its hashes. The dependency Release
was independently regenerated and verified by GitHub Actions.

The package smoke test runs headlessly with an isolated Java user-home directory.
It generates a temporary PKCS#12 test key, signs a text file in CAdES format,
checks the cryptographic signature with OpenSSL and compares the recovered
content with the original. `USE=test` enables this check in Portage.

The upstream AutoFirma and Java-WebSocket unit test suites are not run.
No real certificate, browser profile or system trust store is used by the
packaging tests. GUI, real browser transactions and DNIe/smartcard use have not
been tested.

The browser bootstrap tests use real temporary NSS databases and check CA trust,
TLS hostname/IP validation, Java PKCS#12 interoperability, legacy/current and
absolute Firefox paths with spaces, identity reuse, newly created profiles and
non-destructive handling of invalid existing keystores. They run with `USE=test`
and in GitHub Actions. The revision was built and staged with Portage as well.

## Maintaining the Maven archive

Capture the third-party artifacts needed by a successful build and review
their Maven Central origin and checksums before updating the inventory.
Application build outputs must remain excluded. Regenerate with:

```sh
python3 .github/scripts/bundle-maven.py \
  --inventory .github/maven-bundles/autofirma-1.9.2.json \
  --repository /path/to/local/maven/repository \
  --output /path/to/new/autofirma-1.9.2-maven-deps.tar.xz
```

Use `--fetch` with a fresh repository to reproduce the archive directly from
Maven Central. Record the reviewed archive's `bundle_sha256` in the inventory,
add release notes, commit the changes, and push a new `sources-autofirma-VERSION`
tag. The `Publish Maven dependencies` workflow verifies every artifact and
the generated archive before publishing. Keep published assets immutable.

- https://github.com/ctt-gob-es/clienteafirma/tree/v1.9.2
- https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/autofirma
- https://aur.archlinux.org/cgit/aur.git/tree/PKGBUILD?h=autofirma

The AUR recipe by Oscar Garcia Amor and its contributors supplied the selected
Java-WebSocket commit, upstream patches and Java 17 requirement. Esparto uses
Gentoo's Java launcher and builds the required AutoFirma modules in one reactor.
The icon and license texts come directly from the upstream source archive.
